newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ says to leave April long-term prime unchanged.
newsitem.headline: IBJ says to leave April long-term prime unchanged.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) said on Tuesday it would leave its long-term prime lending rate for April unchanged at 2.5 percent.
The prime rate is applied to loans of one year and longer to the long-term credit bank's most creditworthy clients.
The long-term prime rate was last cut in December to a record low 2.5 percent from 2.7 percent in November.
IBJ also said it will leave the coupon rate on its April five-year debentures, sold to institutional investors, unchanged from the March issue at 1.6 percent.

IBJ's decision to leave the key lending rate unchanged was in line with the market yield of its 1.6 percent March debenture, which was traded at a yield of 1.68 percent on Tuesday morning, bond traders said.
Long-term prime lending rates in Japan are customarily set 0.9 percentage point above the coupon of the benchmark five-year debenture issued monthly by IBJ.

The other two long-term credit banks -- Nippon Credit Bank Ltd and Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd -- are expected to announce their prime lending rates for April and the coupon rates of their April debentures on Wednesday.
